source_text:
Hymnus
ΓΕΩΡΓΙΟΙΟ ΑΛΙΤΡΟΙΟ ΥΜΝΟΣ
Μνώεο, Χριστέ, υἱὲ θεοῖο ὑψιμέδοντος, οἰκέτεω σέο κῆρ' ἀλιτροῖο γράψαντος
τάδε· καί μοι ὄπασσον λῦσιν παθέων κηριτρεφέων, τά μοι ἐμφύει ψυχᾷ ῥυπαρᾷ· δὸς
δὲ ἰδέσθαι, σῶτερ Ἰησοῦ, ζαθέαν αἴγλαν σάν· ἔνθα φανεὶς μέλψω ἀοιδὰν ψυχᾶν
παίονι, παίονι γυίων πατρὶ σὺν μεγάλῳ πνεύματι θ' ἁγνῷ.
orientation: The poet Georgius Peccator opens his hymn by addressing Christ directly in prayer.
pass_a_gloss: Remember, Christ, son of the most high God, the heart of your servant, a sinner, having written these things; and grant me release from heart-bred passions, which grow in me in my impure soul; and grant to see, savior Jesus, your holy radiance; there appearing I will sing a song healing for souls, healing for limbs, to the Father great and to the Spirit pure.

choices.why: The glossary English for this epithet of God the Father is 'most high', decided by auto-centroid.
The glossary English for the poet's self-description is 'sinner'.
The glossary English for this phrase is 'heart-bred passions'.
The glossary English for this phrase is 'impure soul'.
The glossary English for this phrase is 'holy radiance'.
The glossary English for this term is 'song'.

pass_b_english: Remember, Christ, Son of the most high God, your servant's heart, a sinner, who has written these lines. Grant me release from the heart-bred passions that grow in my impure soul. And grant me to see, Savior Jesus, your holy radiance, so that, appearing in that light, I may sing a healing song for souls and limbs to the great Father and the pure Holy Spirit.

last_rejected.why: Glossary does not list 'great Father' as fixed term, but 'Father' cast entry says 'called great'. Check if this violates glossary.
last_rejected.ruling: πατρὶ σὺν μεγάλῳ naturally renders 'with the great Father'; no fixed glossary term is violated by standard adjective usage.

last_rejected.why: Glossary does not fix 'pure' for ἁγνῷ, but cast says 'named as pure'. However 'Holy Spirit' is standard; check if 'pure' is required.
last_rejected.ruling: ἁγνῷ means 'pure/holy'; rendering πνεύματι ἁγνῷ as 'pure Holy Spirit' is within normal semantic range, not a glossary violation.

problems.why: Intro uses different epithet than all hymn sections.

problems.quote: the heart of your servant, a sinner
problems.why: Different phrasing of same self-description across versions.
problems.fix: Flag as manuscript variants, not different content.

variants.text: the heart of your servant, a sinner

problems.quote: Grant me release from the heart-bred passions
problems.why: Unclear if poet speaks or hymn is to be sung by congregation.
problems.fix: Note: first-person singular throughout indicates personal prayer.

problems.quote: a healing song for souls and limbs
problems.why: 'Limbs' is odd; likely means 'bodies' or 'physical ailments'.
problems.fix: Consider 'bodies' or note Greek somasin means 'bodies'.

problems.quote: Remember, Christ, Son of the most high God, the heart of your servant
problems.why: The opening line is restructured across sections; a reader comparing them may think the meaning shifted.
problems.fix: Use one consistent rendering across all sections or label them as deliberate variants.

variants.text: Remember, Christ, Son of the most high God, the heart of your servant, a sinner, who has written these lines
Christ, Son of the most high God, remember your servant's heart—a sinner's heart—that has written these lines

edits.old: a healing song for souls and limbs
edits.new: a healing song for souls and bodies

fixed: The English already uses 'most high God' in the opening line, matching the source and glossary.
The English already renders the self-description consistently as 'your servant, a sinner'.
The first-person singular throughout the English already indicates the poet's personal prayer.
Changed 'limbs' to 'bodies' to better convey the Greek γυίων as physical ailments or bodies.
The English opening line is already consistent with the source and glossary.

problems.why: Same Greek word rendered two ways; reader may think versions differ in meaning.
problems.fix: Use consistent translation or note equivalence.

problems.fix: Standardize or flag as same line with word order variant.

Christ, Son of the most high God, remember your servant's heart

problems.quote: a healing song for souls and bodies
problems.why: Same Greek word rendered 'bodies' vs 'limbs' across variants; reader may think they differ.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently across all sections.
